chapter.title: What Are Design Patterns? Why Use Them?

payload.markdown: So if patterns document good practice, is naming the only truly original thing about pattern catalogs? In some senses, that would seem to be true. Patterns represent best practice in an object-oriented context. To some highly experienced programmers, this may seem an exercise in repackaging the obvious. To the rest of us, patterns provide access to problems and solutions we would otherwise have to discover the hard way.

payload.markdown: Patterns make design accessible. As pattern catalogs emerge for more and more specializations, even the highly experienced can find benefits as they move into new aspects of their fields. A GUI programmer can gain fast access to common problems and solutions in enterprise programming, for example. A web programmer can quickly chart strategies for avoiding the pitfalls that lurk in tablet and smartphone projects.

items: Enterprise Patterns: Patterns for service layers, domain objects and application architecture.
Behavioral Patterns: Patterns that distribute responsibility and coordinate behaviour.
Creational Patterns: Patterns that control how objects come into being.
Design Principles: Guidelines such as SOLID that keep object designs flexible.
Error Patterns: Repeatable strategies: fail fast, wrap and rethrow, aggregate and report.
Factory Pattern: Creating objects through a dedicated creator instead of new at every call site.
HTTP & REST: Designing HTTP endpoints as resources with predictable methods and status codes.
Object Identity: === compares instance identity: two objects with equal fields are still distinct.
